newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian interest rates falling in 97-Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian interest rates falling in 97-Reuter poll.

text.p: Malaysia's three-month Kuala Lumpur interbank offered rate (KLIBOR) will fall, while the ringgit will rise slightly from its present levels against the dollar by the end of 1997, economists said.
In a poll by Reuters, economists from 16 major research houses forecast the three-month KLIBOR will fall to an average 6.9 percent by the end of 1997 from 7.38 percent on Friday.
The benchmark rate is expected to end this year at 7.27 percent against 6.84 on December 29, 1995.
In contrast, the ringgit is expected to gain to around 2.4938 a dollar by the end of 1997 from around 2.5171 at the end of 1996.
Dollar/ringgit was at 2.5265/75 at close on Friday and at 2.5385 on December 29, 1995.
Economists also predicted that expansion of Malaysia's broad monetary aggregates will slow down further over the next year.
